subject: english-literature
source_note: Topic structure follows the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Literature specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Drama
units.blurb: Studying one Modern Drama set play

units.name: Prose
units.blurb: Studying one Modern Prose set novel

units.name: Poetry (anthology)
units.blurb: The named anthology poems and comparison

units.name: Unseen poetry

topics.name: Modern Drama Set Text
topics.blurb: One of A View from the Bridge, The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-time, Kindertransport or Death and the King's Horseman

topics.name: Knowledge & Understanding (AO1)
topics.blurb: Close knowledge of plot, character and theme, supported by textual reference

topics.name: Language, Form & Structure (AO2)
topics.blurb: Analysing dramatic methods: dialogue, stagecraft, structure and their effects

topics.name: Context (AO4)
topics.blurb: Understanding the play in relation to the context in which it was written

topics.name: Modern Prose Set Text
topics.blurb: One of To Kill a Mockingbird, Of Mice and Men, The Whale Rider, The Joy Luck Club or Things Fall Apart

topics.name: Knowledge & Understanding (AO1)
topics.blurb: Close knowledge of the novel maintained in a critical style with apt reference

topics.name: Language, Form & Structure (AO2)
topics.blurb: Analysing narrative voice, language and structure used to create meaning

topics.name: Anthology Poems (Part 3)
topics.blurb: The named set poems in Part 3 of the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE English Anthology

topics.name: Knowledge & Understanding (AO1)
topics.blurb: Close understanding of meaning and the poets' ideas in the anthology poems

topics.name: Language, Form & Structure (AO2)
topics.blurb: Analysing poetic methods, imagery, form and structure and their effects

topics.name: Comparison (AO4)
topics.blurb: Exploring links and connections by comparing two anthology poems

topics.name: Unseen Poem Analysis
topics.blurb: Reading and responding to a previously unseen poem printed in the paper

topics.name: Meaning & Response (AO1)
topics.blurb: Understanding what the poem is about and the response it creates

topics.name: Language, Form & Structure (AO2)
topics.blurb: Analysing the poet's methods and their effects without prior study

connections.why: Secure knowledge of the play is the foundation for analysing how its dramatic methods create meaning
Reading the writer's choices closely opens up how the play reflects the context in which it was written
Studying the set play builds the close knowledge and understanding AO1 assesses
Knowing the novel well underpins analysis of narrative voice, language and structure
Studying the set novel builds the close knowledge AO1 requires
Analysing a dramatist's craft transfers directly to reading a novelist's language and structure
Tracking character and theme across a play develops the same skill for a long prose narrative
Grasping a poem's meaning is the basis for analysing the poetic methods that shape it
Close analysis of each poem's methods is what makes a genuine comparison of two poems possible
Studying the named anthology poems builds the understanding AO1 assesses
Sensitivity to a prose writer's language deepens the analysis of figurative language in poetry
Attention to voice and tone in drama informs the reading of speaker and tone in poems
The close-reading techniques drilled on the named poems are exactly what students apply, unsupported, to an unseen poem
Practice at finding meaning in the anthology builds the instinct needed to make sense of an unseen poem
Responding to an unseen poem is how the meaning-and-response skill of AO1 is demonstrated
Establishing what the poem means anchors the analysis of how its methods create that effect
Comparing poems sharpens the eye for technique that the unseen response draws on under exam conditions
Independent close reading practised on prose strengthens the analytical instinct needed for an unseen poem
